Question: What do you like to do when you are feeling low?
Old_Answer: I plan. I set higher targets for myself. We tend to feel low when things don't go our way. Failures and disappointments are part of life and there should be a way to deal with it. One need break and recreation time to remain but I know when I deserve that break and when I don't. I can't chill watching a movie when I know I haven't completed my targets for the week. See, I can watch a movie, go for an outing, do an episode of emotional eating. There are innumerable ways, but I believe this will distract me for a while but at the of the day, I will have to face the reality and deal with it. There can be any sort of reason for me feeling low. Personal, emotional, academical or whatever. These failures and disappointment ignites something inside and I become more goal oriented. I find my motivation in my failures. I find motivation in rejections. I find motivation in humiliation. I find motivation in disappointments. I find motivation in awkwardness. I find motivation in silence. Negatives get inside me and push me to work harder than before. Constant self doubt and fear of failure keeps me going. Your past situation should never be a deciding factor for your tomorrow. Constantly work on changing your present, so that your tomorrow can be better. If you get comfortable in your present circumstances you will never be able to grow. There is always something inside me that wants change in my current situation and because I want that change, I consciously work for it. Rabiya

I find solace in music that understands my melancholy, letting the melodies wrap around my heart like a warm hug. Sometimes, I let my thoughts spill onto the pages of my diary, where I can pour out my unruly emotions without anyone judging, sort of like a secret friend who nods along without saying a word. And, oh, how I adore talking to my plant—yes, you heard that right! Those little green buddies, they don’t mind if I ramble on about my day; they just listen, gentle and steady, reminding me that it’s okay to be vulnerable. When I’m in this cocoon of comfort, I realize that it’s normal to feel low sometimes—it’s just a part of being human, isn’t it? Question: Do marks really matter in life?
Old_Answer: Yes, marks matter. At some point of time marks matter and after some time it doesn't. Your 10th grade marks will ‘help you’ to decide which stream you want to choose next. Your 12th grade marks will decide your college. Your graduation marks will decide your post graduation or your job or whatever. So, what I am trying to say is ‘marks' do matter. It's just the matter of time. Once you enter college, your 10th grade marks won't matter anymore. Once you complete your graduation, your 12th grade marks won't matter anymore. Image source - Google Now, marks matter in Life? Overall speaking about Life, for some it may matter and for some it may not. There are extremely successful people out there who were not good at academics and also there are people who were extremely good at academics but are not successful. People who want to add value to their life, will add it anyway whether with good marks or bad marks. ~Marks define a phase of your life, it does not define your life.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Marks, in the grand scheme of things, matter but only to a certain extent. Sure, they can open doors and create initial impressions, almost like a shiny badge of honor saying, "Look, I memorized some stuff!" But the truth is, they often fall short of truly defining who you are or what you can accomplish. I mean, take a moment to think about it—there are those who ace exams but can't think outside the box, while others might struggle with grades yet have this inherent brilliance burning inside them, waiting to be unleashed. Life is a rollercoaster ride filled with unexpected twists and turns; your marks are just a tiny blip on that ride. What really matters is the passion you bring, the experiences you gain, and how you translate those into your journey. In the end, it’s about learning, growing, and finding your unique way to shine, regardless of the numbers printed on a piece of paper. So, relax! Give your best, but don’t let those marks weigh you down. Rabiya 💖
Answer_with_user_profile: Marks can often seem like the sole measure of a person's abilities, particularly in the academically-driven society we live in. However, while they do hold some significance—especially in educational opportunities and initial job placements—they are not the definitive factor for success in life. In my experience, particularly here in India, I've observed that many individuals with average or below-average marks excel in their careers due to their practical skills, creativity, perseverance, and interpersonal abilities. Employers frequently look for qualities such as problem-solving skills, communication, and adaptability, which cannot be quantified by marks alone. Moreover, life is filled with numerous avenues for success outside traditional educational systems. Networking, hands-on experience, and continuous learning often outweigh the importance of mere numbers on a report card. Additionally, focusing solely on grades can lead to immense pressure and anxiety, stifling creativity and passion. Therefore, while marks may help open doors, they do not dictate one's entire journey. Those who strive for holistic development—embracing challenges, building relationships, and seeking experiences—are often the ones who thrive in the long run. Ultimately, life is about balance: valuing academic achievements while also nurturing personal growth and practical skills can lead to a fulfilling and successful life.
Answer_with_full_information: Marks, undoubtedly, play a significant role in shaping our educational journey and can heavily influence opportunities in life. However, it's essential to understand that they are not the sole determinants of success or fulfillment. In our society, marks often serve as a benchmarking tool used by educational institutions and employers alike. A high score can open doors to prestigious colleges and job placements, but it is not an absolute reflection of an individual's capabilities or potential. Many successful people, including entrepreneurs and artists, have thrived despite having average or below-average academic performances. What truly matters are the skills we acquire, our ability to adapt, and how we apply our knowledge in real-world scenarios. Moreover, marks can create undue pressure, leading to stress and anxiety among students, which can stifle creativity and passion. It's vital to cultivate a mindset that values learning and personal growth over a mere numerical score. Emphasizing holistic development, including soft skills like communication, teamwork, and problem-solving, often proves more beneficial in the long run. In a rapidly changing world, employers seek individuals who can think critically and innovate, traits that are not always reflected in academic marks. So, while they matter to some extent, remember that marks are just one piece of the puzzle, and focusing on continuous learning and trying new experiences is what really paves the way for a fulfilling life. Honestly, your passion, resilience, and relationships can often eclipse the significance of those numbers on a report card.

Question: What motivates you to study and why?
Old_Answer: I wasn't studying since four days because I had to complete my court internship diary and submit it in the university. I was busy doing that. I was lying on my bed, awake. I got up suddenly and rushed to my study table. Today, I was just procrastinating without any reason. I was finding reasons to not study. I told myself that I am really tired and I should take a break. I am not doing well, emotionally as well. The tornado that has emerged inside me, I don't know how to settle it down. All I can do is cry and weep for a while and get back to work. I knew I just want to beat this initial resistance and then I would be fine. I knew that once I reach my study table, I would not get up before completing atleast one chapter. And without getting a second thought, I threw my quilt away, sat on the chair, turned the laptop on, opened the book and started studying. Just after 10 minutes, my mom came and she kept her palm on my hand and gently started stroking my hairs. She started reciting some verse from Quran and probably was praying that I pass my exams. I don't know, what hit me but tears rolled down my cheeks. I wanted to hug my mom and cry. But I didn't. Maybe I never would. I just can't. Sometimes we get lost. Lost in the future. Lost in the past. Lost in the people who left. Lost in the people who are to come. I study late till night many atimes. Whenever I don't know what to do in life. When the fear of failure hits me hard that I end up crying my soul out, when the uncertain future to come, scares me to hell, I just go and stand outside my parents room. I just see them.
